primitives.meaning: an onboarding decision that depends on a named role or use-case, with no reliable value available for it
entryFilters: an onboarding decision that depends on a named role or use-case, with no reliable value available for it
no instance of this journey is already open for the person or account plus the onboarding context being decided
hard gates (GLB-31) allow communication for this purpose

primitives.asks: Does a reliable declared value already exist?

branches.label: Already declared
branches.test: the person has stated it before and the answer is still current

branches.label: Not declared
branches.test: nothing declared exists - only behaviour, which is not the same thing and is not stored as if it were

primitives.does: Use the existing declared value and record that it was reused rather than re-asked - asking again for something already given is its own small failure

primitives.asks: Would the answer materially change the path to value?

branches.label: Yes
branches.test: different answers lead to genuinely different setup, examples or first actions

branches.label: No
branches.test: the path is the same whatever they answer - the question would be collected and never used

primitives.reEntry: if a later decision genuinely turns on the answer, it is asked then - each question earns its place at the moment it is needed

orderedRoles.eligibleWhen: the message has to be kept and survive until the person can act on it
the person is active in the product and the action is taken there

primitives.purpose: Ask one lightweight question covering only what the implementation will actually consume.
primitives.brief: Ask one lightweight question covering only what the implementation will actually consume. Onboarding does not become a questionnaire on the way to the thing the person came for
primitives.label: CANONICAL_RULE

cancelOn.meaning: the person answers the question that was put to them

primitives.reads: the person or account plus the onboarding context being decided re-read from the system of record before acting on the timeout

primitives.does: Persist the declared value with its source and the time it was given, in a field that only ever holds declared answers. Behavioural inference lives in its own field and is never written here - once the two are mixed, nothing downstream can tell what the person actually said
Continue on a documented default path and record that no declared value exists. The default is not written into the declared field as though someone had chosen it
Adapt the recommended setup, the examples, the next action and the education to the declared context - which is the only reason the question was worth asking

primitives.on: the onboarding path resolved, adapted or defaulted
carries: the declared value with its source, or the explicit fact that there is none
which adaptations were applied, so they are not applied twice
